caption:
Mexico City's Cathedral was deliberately built on top of the Aztecs' most sacred temple — and one of its famous pyramids is 1,000 years older than the people everyone credits it to. 👀

Comment your guess for which one before you swipe ⬇️

1. Metropolitan Cathedral
When the Spanish conquered Tenochtitlan, they tore down the Aztecs' most sacred temple and built the Cathedral on the exact same spot — a deliberate move to erase one religion and plant another in its place.

2. Angel of Independence
The Angel of Independence is bronze sheeted in genuine 24-karat gold. It's fallen once — a 1957 earthquake knocked the statue clean off its column, shattering it into pieces.

3. Chapultepec Castle
The castle became home to Emperor Maximilian I and Empress Carlota in the 1860s. Decades earlier, it was the site of a US Army siege in 1847 — Mexican cadets as young as 13 died defending it.

4. UNAM
Founded in 1551, UNAM / Royal University became the first university in the Americas — almost a century before Harvard existed, while most of North America hadn't even seen a European settler yet.

5. The sinking city
Mexico City was built over a lake the Aztecs drained centuries ago. The old lakebed is still settling under the weight of the modern city, so the ground quite literally sinks beneath your feet — up to 20 inches a year in some areas.

6. Paseo de la Reforma
In the 1860s, Mexico's emperor wanted a grand boulevard to rival Europe's capitals, so Paseo de la Reforma was designed in the style of the Champs-Élysées — and it's stayed the city's most elegant avenue ever since.

7. Teotihuacan
Teotihuacan, located about an hour from Mexico City, was built over 1,000 years before the Aztecs even arrived in the region. When the Aztecs found the abandoned city centuries later, they were so stunned they assumed it was built by gods.
